—— Your government ——

Delhi is managing weeks of tools against months of disruption.

Government Response

Delhi is rationing, escorting, and freezing prices. It expects months, not weeks.

Policy posture signals a prolonged standoff is the base case, not a short disruption.

01
Supply rationing & price controls activated
ESMA (Essential Commodities Act) invoked. Commercial LPG capped at 20% above baseline allocation. Retail fuel prices frozen across all OMC (Oil Marketing Company) outlets.
ESMA INVOKED LPG CAP +20% PRICES FROZEN
02
Naval escorts deployed for tanker protection
6–7 Indian Navy warships repositioned for escort operations on key Persian Gulf and Indian Ocean crude supply lanes.
6–7 WARSHIPS ACTIVE ESCORT OPS
03
Planning horizon set at 90+ days
Internal guidance designates Prolonged Standoff as the base case scenario at 60% probability, with a duration assumption exceeding 90 days.
60% BASE CASE 90+ DAYS
The simultaneous use of statutory rationing, military assets, and an extended planning horizon indicates the government does not expect a near-term resolution. Boards should model procurement, hedging, and logistics against a minimum 90-day disruption window.

Source: Working Document Section E23, C14, G33  ·  ESMA = Essential Commodities Act; LPG = Liquefied Petroleum Gas; OMC = Oil Marketing Company

Source: Working Document Section B6 · CAD = Current Account Deficit

Convergence Risk

Three deadlines converge before April 6. Your board is planning for none of them.

72-hour window · Supply, pricing, and contingency gaps align simultaneously

Key takeaway: Three independent risk triggers collide in one 72-hour window
Critical procurement, supply, and governance deadlines · April 3–6, 2026
APR 3 Russia Crude Waiver Expires
Preferential pricing arrangement lapses. No confirmed replacement crude source. 30M bbl/month exposure at market spot rates.
APR 5 OPEC+ Meeting
Planned output increase: +206K bbl/d (Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries Plus). Covers roughly 0.2% of global demand — insufficient to offset waiver-driven supply gap.
APR 6 All Three Deadlines Passed
No board contingency plan in place. Supply gap unresolved. OPEC+ increase absorbed by demand. Organisation is now fully exposed on price, volume, and governance.

Board action required before April 3. The OPEC+ increase of 206K bbl/d (bbl/d = barrels per day) does not compensate for the Russia waiver gap. Without a replacement supply contract and a board-approved contingency, the organisation enters April 6 with three unresolved risk vectors simultaneously active.

Source: Working Document Section F27, F28

Price vs. Reality

A ceasefire announcement removes the political risk premium — but not the physical one. Strait of Hormuz mine clearance requires dedicated minesweepers (currently thousands of miles away), a verified cessation of hostilities, and 8–12 weeks of clearance operations. Markets that priced in full re-opening on the announcement will face a correction as operational constraints become apparent.

Source: Working Document Section D18, A8
